content: Spirulina, also known as blue-green algae, has specific dosing recommendations based on its intended use. For general supplementation, a dose of 1 gram taken orally once daily for 12 days is suggested. Alternatively, 1500 mg of Super Blue-Green Algae (SBGA) capsules can be taken orally. Spirulina is recognized as a source of protein, iron, and B vitamins. It has been found effective for managing oral leukoplakia and may help increase energy and metabolism. However, while it is an effective source of protein and iron, it is relatively expensive when compared gram-for-gram to conventional food sources. Spirulina is likely effective for treating leukoplakia but is possibly ineffective as a source of vitamin B12 or as a weight-loss aid. Contamination with microcystin, a toxin, is a potential concern. Adverse effects associated with Spirulina include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hepatotoxicity (liver toxicity), shock, and hypersensitivity reactions. It is contraindicated in individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific categorization available (Pregnancy Category: N/A; Lactation: N/A). However, Spirulina is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
